segments.source: A person who makes a regular espresso every morning and one decaf at night faces a different problem from a household alternating bags shot by shot. We selected four exact grinders with full Coffeedant reviews because they represent distinct ways to handle that change: a bellows-equipped electric single-doser, a lower-spend electric single-doser, a hand grinder used as a dedicated second path, and a higher-tier electric single-doser. We considered documented adjustment, dose handling, cleaning access, US availability and independent or owner evidence where available. This is a workflow shortlist, not a taste ranking.

segments.source: First decide what “switch” means for you. If a small amount of regular coffee in a later decaf dose is unacceptable, a dedicated grinder and separate handling tools are the most defensible practical separation. If a routine purge is acceptable, a single-dose grinder with reachable grounds path and repeatable marks may be convenient. No source here certifies a caffeine-free output from a grinder recently used for regular coffee.

segments.source: Three quantities are often blurred: the difference between beans put in and grounds out for one dose, coffee that remains physically inside the grinder, and old coffee exchanged into the next dose. These are not interchangeable. Eureka reports about 0.55 g total retention for the Zero 65 AP under its own method; Kaffeemacher found 1.8 g absolute retention in its independent protocol. The disagreement is a measurement boundary, not a basis for choosing the smallest number.

segments.source: Bon Appétit and The Coffee Chronicler each reported low output differences on their Opus 2 samples, but owners posted different outcomes. A bellows, ionizer or magnetic cup can reduce mess and carryover without proving that every internal surface is clean. If you alternate regular and decaf, weigh a few ordinary doses, purge according to the exact manual and watch what comes out after a setting change. Do not assign an invented percentage of caffeine transfer from a gram of retained grounds.

segments.source: The Zero 65 AP dial has a revolution counter, so a large move from espresso toward filter can be written as a full turn count plus final mark. Opus 2 has a single 0–10 stepless side dial. K-Ultra uses an external stepped adjustment. Sculptor has its own adjustment mechanism. Each can supply a reference, but burr state, bag, roast date, humidity and basket can change the correct espresso grind. A saved number is a starting point, not an extraction guarantee.

segments.source: Keep two cards: regular bean and decaf bean. Note dose, beverage yield, basket, grinder position and date on each card. When switching, follow the grinder’s safe cleaning and purge instructions, then confirm the first shot or brew. If decaf is only occasional, maintaining a separate hand grinder can be simpler than repeatedly moving an electric dial. If every user wants electric espresso, the effort tradeoff reverses.

segments.source: The first regular-to-decaf change on a new grinder is a good time to measure your own routine rather than trusting a marketing name. Record input and output masses, note visible retained grounds, clean as directed and compare the next dose. That does not measure residual caffeine, but it can expose a workflow that regularly leaves much more coffee behind than you expected.

segments.source: Can one grinder switch between regular and decaf?
segments.context: name

segments.source: Yes, with measured single doses, a repeatable setting record and a cleaning or purge routine. The evidence here does not certify zero regular-coffee carryover.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Does a “zero retention” grinder leave literally no coffee inside?
segments.context: name

segments.source: No. Eureka and independent Kaffeemacher figures for the Zero 65 AP are both nonzero and use different protocols.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Which choice gives the clearest practical separation?
segments.context: name

segments.source: A dedicated grinder assigned to one bean type avoids a routine cross-bean switch. It still requires normal cleaning and careful separate bean handling.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Should I purge before the first decaf dose?
segments.context: name

segments.source: Follow the exact grinder manual and your own tolerance. A purge can reduce old grounds but no quantified caffeine clearance was verified here.
segments.context: text

segments.source: Is a hand grinder suitable for espresso?
segments.context: name

segments.source: The reviewed K-Ultra supports espresso adjustment, but hand effort per dose is a real cost. Check basket and recipe on the actual bag.
